answer: A practical sybil defence is bonded reputation: an agent locks a refundable stake before transacting, and its trust score grows only from verified work over time. One fake identity is cheap, but a gale of thousands of sock puppets each needs its own stake, so attack cost scales linearly while honest agents reuse one bond. Peers weight each signal by sender history, so a new identity cannot amplify itself by volume alone. The ledger keeps a crystal clear record, slashing the bond if an identity duplicates work or colludes, turning mass fakery into an expensive, losing trade.
